en.title: Minimum Operations to Make Arrays Equal
en.description:
Given integer arrays source and target of equal length. One operation chooses a prefix or a suffix and adds 1 to every element in it. Find the minimum number of operations; output −1 if source cannot be turned into target.

This site uses a standard input/output protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains source; the third line contains target. 1≤n≤100000, and every element's absolute value is ≤10^13.
en.output: Output the minimum number of operations, or −1.
en.explanation: Let d[i]=target[i]−source[i], which must be non-negative everywhere. Each drop from d[i−1] to d[i] needs at least one prefix operation ending at that boundary. If the total drop N exceeds d[0], it is impossible; otherwise, N prefix operations plus some suffix/whole-array operations make up the rest, and the minimum number of operations is d[n−1]+N.
